To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

two natural dihydroxybenzenes, 2,3- and 2, 5-dihydroxybenzoic acids, are chemosensitising compounds that enhance the activity of the antifungal drug Amphotericin-B against Candida and Cryptocooccus species.

dihydroxybenzoic acid derivatives, which are natural products that can target the oxidative stress response of fungi, can enhance antifungal activity of amphotericicin B against Candida and Cryptoccocus species.

the redox-potent DHBAs (2,3-DHBAs and 2,4-DHBAs) are chemosensitizes to AMB in vitro through co-disruption (or inhibition) of the yeast mitochondrial superoxide dismutation system, which is a component of the cellular oxidative stress response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel antifungal agents and/or the enhancement of existing antifungal agents.
understanding the mechanisms of action of natural products and their potential for chemosensitizating antifungal drugs.
the discovery and development of novel, redox-potent, chemosensitising compounds that can enhance the efficacy of the antifungal drug, AMB, in the treatment of fungal infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DHBAs are promising chemosensitising agents to AMB against Candida spp. and C. neoformans.

dihydroxybenzylic compounds are potent chemosensitive to amphotericin b through co-disruption the oxidative stress response of yeasts, which shows promise for enhancing amphotericin based antifungal therapy of candidiasis and cryptocoocosis.
the redox-potent dihydroxybenzenes (2,3- and 2, 5-DHBA) were found to be potent chemosensitizer to AMB through the co-disruption of oxidative stress response in yeasts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we identified four natural benzaldehydes, two dihydroxybenzyldes (2,3-DHBAs and 2,4-DHBAs) and two nonhydroxybenzaldhydes (trans-cinnamaldehydes and 3,5-dimetoxbenzaldhyde), that have chemosensitizating activities to amphotericin (AMB) against four Candida and Cryptosoccus strains.

the redox-potency of certain natural compounds can be harnessed in combination with AMBs to enhance their antifungal activities, and this chemosensitisation is due to disruption of the cellular redox homeostasis of yeasts.
the combination of AMB and DHBAs is a promising therapeutic strategy against fungal infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxidative stress response is a viable target in AMB-based antipathogen therapy.
redox-potent dihydroxybenzenes are promising chemosensitiziers for AMB.
certain redox-active compounds can chemosensitize AMB through co-targeting the oxidative stress response system in fungi.
